start.name: Mostorod (Mostorod refining/petrochemical industrial area)
start.coord_basis: OSM landuse=industrial way 28830035 'Mostorod', Shubra El-Kheima district, Al-Qalyubia governorate, north Cairo — matches sheet StartLocation='Mostorud'/StartState/Province='Al-Qalyubia'. This is the Mostorod refinery/petrochemical hub the Arabic name references.

end.name: El Tebbin (El Tebbin Power Station / steel-cement industrial complex, Helwan)
end.coord_basis: OSM landuse=industrial way 502404024 'محطة كهرباء التبين' (El Tebbin Power Station), Helwan district, Cairo governorate, south Cairo. Chosen over the sheet's EndPrefecture/District cell (which erroneously repeats 'Mostorud') because the Arabic OtherLanguagePrimaryPipelineName 'خط غاز مستطرد-- التبين' unambiguously names El Tebbin (التبين) as the terminus, not Mostorod again. Independently cross-checked: this coordinate coincides with the endpoint GEM's own existing operating pipeline P8021 (Kuraimat-Al Tebbin) uses for its El Tebbin terminus (internal consistency check only, not cited as a source).

corridor_desc: If real at full length, the line would run from the Mostorod refining/petrochemical hub (Qalyubia, far north Cairo) south through greater Cairo to the El Tebbin steel/cement/power complex (Helwan, far south Cairo) — i.e. spanning the entire Cairo metro area north-to-south, likely following the east or west desert-fringe road/rail corridor rather than threading downtown. NOTE: this corridor length is fundamentally in tension with the sheet's stated 25 km (see flags) — a genuine Mostorod-Tebbin gas line at this length would need to be a much longer, differently-routed line than what '25 km' implies, or the sheet's endpoints/length do not both refer to the full city-spanning route.

facts.source: Could not independently confirm length/diameter/year for this specific line; see flags on citation.

flags: endpoint-mismatch: sheet's EndPrefecture/District cell reads 'Mostorud' (same as StartLocation) — this is almost certainly a data-entry error; the Arabic OtherLanguagePrimaryPipelineName ('...التبين') clearly names El Tebbin, not Mostorod, as the true terminus.

length-implausible: straight-line distance between Mostorod and El Tebbin (OSM industrial-area anchors) is ~40.8 km, i.e. 1.63x LONGER than the sheet's stated 25.00 km — a real pipeline route can only be equal to or longer than the straight-line distance between its endpoints, so 25 km is not geometrically possible for these two termini. Baird's own estimate in the brief ('straight line is roughly 30 km') undershot the actual figure (40.8 km), making the discrepancy worse, not better, than suspected.

citation-unverified: the cited seed source (EGAS Annual Report 2018, both live and Wayback-snapshot copies) was full-text-searched (pdftotext) for 'Mostorod'/'Mostorud'/'Tebbin'/'Tabbin' and no matching line item was found in its national-grid pipeline tables (searched 'COMPLETED DURING 2017/2018' and 'UNDER CONSTRUCTION' sections, pp.35-37 of the extracted text) — the Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Diameter/Length refs on this row all point to this same PDF, none independently confirmed.

unverified-existence: found no independent secondary source (news, GASCO/EGAS materials, trade press) describing a natural-gas pipeline specifically between Mostorod and El Tebbin at any length; a DIFFERENT, unrelated fuel-oil/mazut pipeline realignment between the same two places (19 km segment, $4.2M, targeted for 2027) is reported by africaoilgasreport.com (Aug 2026), confirming an industrial linkage between the two hubs exists but for a different commodity/system, not corroborating this gas line's existence, length, or diameter.

possible-redundancy-check: GEM already has P8021 'Kuraimat-Al Tebbin Gas Pipeline' (87 km, operating) terminating at the same El Tebbin locality from a different (southern, Beni Suef-side) origin — not a duplicate of P8057 (different start point and corridor), but worth a human cross-check for whether both are real, distinct lines feeding El Tebbin.
notes: Resolved the START/END DIRECTION with high confidence: the sheet's EndPrefecture/District='Mostorud' is a clear copy-paste/data-entry error, and the Arabic name settles it as Mostorod->El Tebbin, consistent with the user's brief. However, I could NOT resolve or corroborate the stated 25 km length, and could not independently verify the pipeline's existence/attributes at all beyond the sheet's own (apparently mis-cited) EGAS 2018 reference. Straight-line Mostorod-Tebbin is 40.8 km (ratio 1.63x over stated length) -- geometrically the stated length is impossible for these two full-city endpoints. Two ways to reconcile, neither of which I can adjudicate from available sources: (a) the 25 km figure is simply wrong/should be revised upward (~41+ km straight line, more once routed), or (b) the true endpoints are NOT the full Mostorod industrial area and El Tebbin power station, but nearer, more localized points sharing those place names (e.g. a shorter tie-in segment) that I have no way to identify without the actual source document. Given I also could not find the line item in the cited 2018 EGAS report itself, I recommend this row get a full Update-workflow source pass (existence + length + diameter) before route geometry is drawn, not just an endpoint fix. Confidence tier: low (single, unverified source; direction inferred from the Arabic name only, not corroborated elsewhere).

start.name: Dahshur (Manshaat Dahshur / GASCO Dahshur compressor-station locality)
start.coord_basis: OSM place=village node 768779115 'منشأة دهشور' (Manshaat Dahshur), Giza governorate — the settlement adjoining GASCO's Dahshur compressor station, which the seed press release itself names as undergoing an unrelated expansion ('توسعات محطة ضواغط دهشور') in the same paragraph that lists the 67 km duplication project. Matches sheet StartLocation='Dahshour'/StartState/Province='Giza'.

end.name: New Administrative Capital (primary hypothesis — see flags for the contested alternative)
end.coord_basis: OSM place=city node 7152775457 'العاصمة الإدارية الجديدة' (the New Administrative Capital). Chosen as the PRIMARY hypothesis over 'Cairo proper' because: (1) the seed source itself, read at the raw Arabic ('مشروع ازدواج خط العاصمة/ دهشور بطول 67 كم' — 'duplication of the Capital/Dahshur line, 67 km'), and P8058's own Arabic name ('خط غاز العاصمة- دهشور 2') both put العاصمة (Capital) BEFORE دهشور — the same word order GEM's own existing P3930 'New Administrative Capital–Dahshur Gas Pipeline' uses ('العاصمة الجديدة - دهشور'), NOT the reversed order P8040 'Dahshour-Cairo Gas Pipeline' uses ('دهشور-العاصمة'); (2) a straight line from this Dahshur anchor to the NAC anchor is 55.7 km against the sheet's stated 67 km (ratio 1.20x — geometrically plausible for a real corridor), whereas a straight line from the same Dahshur anchor to the P8040-corridor's own Cairo/Giza terminus is only 33.7 km against the same 67 km (ratio 1.99x — implausibly short, would require an unrealistic amount of winding). See flags for why this contradicts the row's English name.

corridor_desc: PRIMARY hypothesis: a second/parallel ('duplication', ازدواج) transmission line alongside GEM's existing operating P3930 (New Administrative Capital–Dahshur Gas Pipeline, 70 km, 32in, completed July 2017 per the EGAS 2018 annual report), running from the Dahshur GASCO compressor station east-northeast across the desert to the New Administrative Capital area (which needs the added gas capacity for its power station, per multiple sources on P3930). ALTERNATIVE hypothesis (see flags): a second/parallel line alongside P8040 (Dahshour-Cairo Gas Pipeline, 65 km, medium-accuracy mapped route already in the routes repo), running from the same Dahshur station west/northwest into the Cairo/Giza urban gas network near the Royal City area of Giza governorate. Both are physically short trips from the same Dahshur compressor-station origin; the government's 2022 announcement text is not specific enough on its own to fully disambiguate, hence 'resolved: true' here reflects a reasoned primary call, not certainty — see flags.

facts.source: https://www.petroleum.gov.eg/ar-eg/media-center/news/news-pages/Pages/mop_02052022_01.aspx — verified by direct download (curl) and text extraction; confirms '67 km' as a 'ازدواج' (duplication/twinning) project among ~6 billion EGP of future national-grid projects, and separately confirms an unrelated Dahshur compressor-station capacity expansion (27.5→46 million m3/day) in the same release. No diameter given in this source.

flags: corridor-identification-uncertain: the English pipeline name 'Dahshour-Cairo Gas Pipeline II' literally reads as a sequel to P8040 'Dahshour-Cairo Gas Pipeline', but the word order in BOTH P8058's own Arabic name and the seed press release's raw Arabic text puts العاصمة (Capital) before دهشور — matching GEM's existing P3930 'New Administrative Capital–Dahshur Gas Pipeline' (also Capital-then-Dahshur), not P8040 (which is Dahshur-then-Capital). Combined with the straight-line-distance plausibility check (below), the weight of evidence favors this being the SECOND LINE of the P3930 corridor (to the New Administrative Capital), not of the P8040 corridor (to old Cairo) — i.e. the researcher (NA) who added this row may have mis-attributed it to the wrong existing pipeline family when naming it. Recommend human adjudication and a possible rename before route creation proceeds.

length-implausible-for-alternative: IF this is instead the P8040-corridor twin (per the English name), the straight-line Dahshur-to-P8040-terminus distance is only 33.7 km against a stated 67 km (ratio 1.99x) — a very high winding factor for what is mostly flat desert/urban-fringe terrain, and notably higher than P8040's own real mapped route's winding factor (54.8 km mapped vs 31.7 km straight-line = 1.73x). This physical implausibility is itself evidence against the P8040-corridor reading.

length-plausible-for-primary: the NAC-corridor hypothesis's straight-line-to-stated-length ratio (55.7 km vs 67 km stated = 1.20x) is much more consistent with a real transmission-line routing than the P8040-corridor alternative, reinforcing the primary call above.

diameter-unstated: sheet leaves Diameter blank for P8058, unlike its P8040 (24,20in) and P3930 (32in) neighbors — worth flagging as a gap for the Update workflow, not something this endpoint pass can fill.
notes: This is a genuinely ambiguous row and I want to be explicit that 'resolved: true' reflects a reasoned primary call, not a confirmed fact. Evidence assembled: (1) EGAS Annual Report 2018 (verified, Wayback fallback used since egyptoil-gas.com timed out live) confirms 'New Capital / Dahshur Pipeline 70 km - 32in', completed July 2017 -- this is GEM's own P3930, corroborating that a real 'Capital-Dahshur' line already exists at ~70 km, very close to P8058's stated 67 km. (2) The 2022 petroleum.gov.eg press release (verified, read via curl+text-extraction of the raw Arabic, not just an AI paraphrase) explicitly calls the 67 km project a 'ازدواج' (duplication/twinning), i.e. a second parallel pipe alongside an EXISTING line -- and P8058's status='construction' (vs P3930's 'operating') is fully consistent with P8058 being that twin, built years after the original. (3) Both P8058's own Arabic name and the press release's Arabic text order العاصمة before دهشور, matching P3930's naming convention rather than P8040's reversed order -- a linguistic clue the English pipeline-name obscures. (4) Straight-line-to-stated-length plausibility clearly favors the NAC corridor (1.20x) over the P8040 corridor (1.99x). Given all four lines of evidence point the same direction and none contradict it, I resolved end=New Administrative Capital, but flagged the naming conflict explicitly so a human can override if there's context I don't have (e.g. a GASCO planning document that explicitly ties this specific construction project to P8040 instead). I could not reach the presidency.eg project page (title: 'إنشاء خط غاز العاصمة الجديدة - دهشور (سيمينز)', which appears to be about the ORIGINAL P3930 line's Siemens/Turboden compressor buildout, not P8058) -- it 403s directly and has no Wayback snapshot; a jina.ai reader proxy returned only nav-menu boilerplate, no article body, so I did not cite it. Confidence tier: medium (2 independent, verified sources -- the 2018 EGAS report for the P3930 baseline and the 2022 ministry release for the duplication project -- corroborate the EXISTENCE and approximate length of a Capital/Dahshur duplication effort, but neither source explicitly disambiguates which 'Capital' terminus by name).
